tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteProPGrou.summary: Tau Ceti already contains most of Layers 0–3: profinite quotients, the unbundled limit description and completion universal property, supernatural numbers with order, index and Lagrange, profinite Sylow existence, conjugacy and maximality, the maximal pro-p quotient, finiteness and countability of open subgroups, the Hopf property, continuous sections for closed subgroups, and the pro-p Frattini subgroup with its verbal description and the Burnside basis theorem; its roadmap STATUS.md (1 September) is out of date on all of this. Also present are inputs the later layers treat as work: Tau Ceti's abstract extension/H² dictionary and explicit low-degree continuous cohomology (H¹ ≅ continuous homomorphisms, (1,1) cup product with graded commutativity, Shapiro in degrees 0–1, cor∘res in degrees 0–2), and Mathlib's Weierstrass division over complete local rings, power-series evaluation, topological abelianization, Erdős–Kaplansky and the Amice transform. Genuinely missing: topological generator rank and convergent generating sets, Gaschütz and Schreier bounds, every free profinite, pro-C and pro-p object and presentation, Ẑ, ℤ_p-module structure on abelian pro-p groups, embedding problems and projectivity, cohomological dimension, the lower p-series, completed group algebras, and all Demushkin theory and classification.

targets.target: Instance chain: a totally disconnected topological group is T1, T2 and T3, so no statement needs [T2Space G]
targets.note: Instance search already derives T1 (priority-100 instance from total disconnectedness), regularity of every topological group, T3 from T0 plus regular, and T2 from T3; the Tau Ceti file Profinite/Basic.lean records in its module doc that no glue instance is needed.

targets.target: G ⧸ N is profinite for G profinite and N closed normal (TotallyDisconnectedSpace (G ⧸ N) by the clopen-image argument, with the compact and topological-group instances)
targets.note: Tau Ceti supplies the missing total disconnectedness (instance argument IsClosed N) exactly by the clopen-image argument; Mathlib supplies compactness (anonymous instance at Quotient.lean:36), the topological-group structure and T3. There is no bundled ProfiniteGrp quotient by a closed normal subgroup, which the layer does not ask for.

targets.target: A closed subgroup of a profinite group is profinite
targets.note: Bundled form; the unbundled instances are the CompactSpace instance for a ClosedSubgroup (Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Group/ClosedSubgroup.lean) and Subtype.totallyDisconnectedSpace.

targets.target: An element lying in every open normal subgroup is 1
targets.note: Stated for compact totally disconnected topological groups (namespace TauCeti with _root_ names).

targets.target: A subgroup is open if and only if it is closed of finite index
targets.note: Both directions are in Mathlib as separate lemmas (closed plus FiniteIndex gives open; open gives closed and, for compact G, a finite quotient); no single iff is packaged. Tau Ceti states the supernatural-index form used in Layer 1.

targets.target: Open normal subgroups of G ⧸ N correspond to open normal subgroups of G containing N
targets.note: An order isomorphism for any topological group and normal N (closedness not needed).

targets.target: Unbundled inverse-limit description: a compatible family in the finite quotients comes from a unique element
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the unbundled statement for compact totally disconnected groups; Mathlib has the bundled bijection with the limit of the finite-quotient diagram.

targets.target: Compactness lemma: a directed family of nonempty closed subsets of a profinite (compact) space has nonempty intersection
targets.note: Cantor's intersection theorem for directed families of compact closed sets (Mathlib) and its CompactSpace wrapper (Tau Ceti); Mathlib also has nonemptiness of cofiltered limits of nonempty finite sets.

targets.target: Unbundled universal property of the profinite completion: continuous homomorphisms from the completion to a profinite P correspond to homomorphisms from G
targets.note: Tau Ceti restates the Mathlib adjunction for unbundled groups; G and P must lie in the same universe.

targets.target: The unit G → completion is bijective for finite G
targets.note: Proved from dense range and residual finiteness of finite groups.

targets.target: Supernatural numbers Nat.Primes → ℕ∞ with divisibility as ≤, multiplication as pointwise +, lattice operations, the embedding of ℕ+, the "is natural" predicate, p-primary and prime-to-p parts
targets.note: CompleteLattice and CommMonoid instances (multiplication adds exponents), primePower including p^∞, IsNatural; built for exactly this milestone.

targets.target: API: ofNat multiplicative and injective, sending gcd and lcm to ⊓ and ⊔; a supernatural number is natural iff it has finite support and finite values
targets.note: Also ofNat_dvd_ofNat_iff and ofNatMonoidHom.

targets.target: profiniteOrder G as a supernatural number; on a finite discrete group it is the factorization of Nat.card G
targets.note: Defined as the supremum over open normal subgroups of the valuations of the quotient orders, for any topological group.

targets.target: profiniteIndex H G primewise through finite quotients; for closed H it equals the supremum of [G : U] over open U ≥ H; invariance under closure; index 1 iff dense (iff H = ⊤ for closed H)
targets.note: The open-overgroup description holds for arbitrary H in a compact topological group, so it is more general than the closed case the layer asks for.

targets.target: Index API: invariance under topological isomorphism, multiplicativity in towers of closed subgroups, image formula under continuous surjections, Lagrange order G = order H · index, agreement with Subgroup.index for open H
targets.note: The image formula is index(f K) = index(K ⊔ ker f) for a continuous surjection of compact groups; the tower law is also stated as Subgroup.profiniteIndex_mul_profiniteIndex (Index/Transitivity.lean:74).

targets.target: G is pro-p iff profiniteOrder G is supported at p; H is open iff closed of natural-number index
targets.note: Needs [Fact p.Prime] and a compact group with separately continuous multiplication.

targets.target: Worked values: the order of ℤ_p is p^∞ and the order of Ẑ is ∏_ℓ ℓ^∞
targets.note: profiniteOrder is not applied to any concrete group in either library (grep for profiniteOrder outside Profinite/ finds only a docstring in Supernatural.lean); Ẑ itself does not exist (grep for ZHat, Ẑ, ℤ̂, "profinite integers" finds only prose).

targets.target: IsProPSylow p P (closed, pro-p, index prime to p in each finite quotient) and its equivalence with ¬ p ∣ profiniteIndex P G; agreement with Mathlib Sylow on finite groups
targets.note: The comparison with Mathlib Sylow needs only a discrete group and P of finite index, not a finite group. Mathlib has no profinite Sylow notion.

targets.target: Existence of a p-Sylow subgroup in every profinite group, including the constructor from a compatible family of Sylow subgroups of the finite quotients
targets.note: Proved by the inverse-limit argument over the finite sets of Sylow subgroups of the finite quotients, as the layer prescribes.

targets.target: Conjugacy of p-Sylow subgroups; every closed pro-p subgroup lies in a p-Sylow; maximal pro-p iff Sylow; a normal p-Sylow is unique
targets.note: Containment holds for every pro-p subgroup, closed or not. The README frozen surface names IsProPSylow.eq_of_normal and IsProP.exists_le_isProPSylow, which exist under namespace TauCeti.

targets.target: The image of a p-Sylow subgroup under a continuous surjection is p-Sylow
targets.note: Only the isomorphism case (and conjugation, IsProPSylow.map_conj) is stated; the ingredients for surjections (index cannot increase, pro-p passes to images) exist, but the frozen-surface name IsProPSylow.map_of_surjective does not.

targets.target: The p-Sylow subgroup of an inverse limit is the inverse limit of p-Sylow subgroups
targets.note: Only the system of G's own finite quotients is covered; nothing is stated for an arbitrary inverse system of profinite groups or for ProfiniteGrp.limit.

targets.target: Every p-Sylow subgroup of Ẑ is topologically isomorphic to ℤ_p
targets.note: Neither library defines Ẑ (the profinite completion of ℤ is never instantiated); no statement relates IsProPSylow to PadicInt.

targets.target: IsProP API: stability under closed subgroups, quotients by closed normal subgroups and finite products; agreement with IsPGroup on finite discrete groups
targets.note: Subgroups need not be closed and quotients need not be by closed subgroups; IsProP.prod covers binary products.

targets.target: Stability of pro-p under inverse limits, and pro-p iff continuously isomorphic to a limit of finite p-groups
targets.note: No statement links IsProP to ProfiniteGrp.limit or to any inverse system (grep for IsProP with limit/iInf/ProfiniteGrp finds nothing).

targets.target: proPKernel and the maximal pro-p quotient: closed, normal, characteristic, pro-p, universal property, idempotence, functoriality
targets.note: Also maximalProPQuotient.map with map_id/map_comp, lift_comp_map/comp_lift naturality, and proPKernel_eq_bot_iff (pro-p iff trivial kernel).

targets.target: Topological generation: IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated and its passage along continuous surjections
targets.note: Tau Ceti also characterizes finite generation by a uniform bound on Group.rank of the finite quotients.

targets.target: ConvergesToOne generating sets, and existence of a generating set converging to 1 in every profinite group
targets.note: grep -i for convergesToOne, "converging to 1" and cofinite-to-𝓝 1 families finds nothing relevant in either tree.

targets.target: topologicalGeneratorRank (cardinal) with monotonicity under surjections, finiteness iff topologically finitely generated, and the ℕ accessor
targets.note: Only the abstract ℕ-valued Group.rank of a finitely generated group exists; no topological generator rank in either library.

targets.target: Finitely many open subgroups of each index in a topologically finitely generated group; countably many open (normal) subgroups; a cofinal descending sequence of open normal subgroups
targets.note: Only compactness is used; with Mathlib IsCompact.nonempty_iInter_of_sequence_nonempty_isCompact_isClosed this gives the sequential compactness lemma.

targets.target: Schreier bound d(U) ≤ 1 + [G : U](d(G) − 1) for open U in a topologically finitely generated profinite group
targets.note: Mathlib has only the weaker abstract bound rank H ≤ index · rank G for finite-index subgroups of finitely generated discrete groups; there is no topological rank to state the profinite bound.

targets.target: Hopf property: a continuous surjective endomorphism of a topologically finitely generated profinite group is an isomorphism
targets.note: Proved by counting open subgroups of each index (Ribes–Zalesskii 2.5.2).

targets.target: Gaschütz lifting of generating n-tuples along continuous surjections, and its Frattini corollary
targets.note: grep -i Gasch finds only gaSchemePointParamMul; neither library has the finite Gaschütz lemma either.

targets.target: Frattini theory for pro-p groups: maximal open subgroups are normal of index p; proPFrattini closed, normal, characteristic, equal to the intersection of maximal open subgroups and to closure(G^p[G,G]); the Frattini quotient is elementary abelian
targets.note: Present: the index-p definition, closedness, the verbal description (for any profinite G), commutative exponent-p quotient, characteristicity and surjective images. Missing: the identification with the intersection of maximal open subgroups (the file doc says it is not established), the statement that a maximal open subgroup of a pro-p group is normal of index p, an 𝔽_p-module structure on the quotient, and comparison with Mathlib frattini.

targets.target: Burnside basis theorem: a subset topologically generates a pro-p group iff its image generates G/Φ(G); a closed subgroup in no index-p open normal subgroup is everything
targets.note: The third Suggested.lean form (a continuous homomorphism surjective onto every index-p quotient is surjective) is not separately stated but follows from the second.

targets.target: Rank identities: d(G) = dim Hom_cont(G, 𝔽_p) as cardinals; G topologically finitely generated iff G/Φ(G) finite; d(G) = finrank of G/Φ(G)
targets.note: No generator rank exists, and no statement relates proPFrattini to finrank or to continuous characters into ZMod p.

targets.target: Worked examples: ℤ_p, ℤ/p^n and free pro-p groups are pro-p; d(ℤ_p) = 1; Φ(ℤ_p) = pℤ_p
targets.note: Only finite p-groups such as ℤ/p^n are covered (IsPGroup.isProP); nothing about ℤ_p or free pro-p groups.

targets.target: FiniteGroupClass (closed under subgroups, quotients, extensions, with Shrink policy); proCKernel, proCCompletion with universal property; finiteGroupClassP p with proCKernel = proPKernel
targets.note: No class of finite groups or pro-C notion in either tree (grep FiniteGroupClass, IsProC, proCKernel, "formation of groups" returns nothing; IsProC hits are IsProConstructible). Only the pro-p instance exists.

targets.target: freeProfiniteGroup X = completion of FreeGroup X with generators and universal property; presentedProfiniteGroup
targets.note: Neither library defines a free profinite or presented profinite group; the universal property would compose the completion adjunction with FreeGroup.lift, both present.

targets.target: freeProC and freeProP with universal properties, uniqueness and functoriality in X; freeProC (finiteGroupClassP p) X ≅ freeProP p X
targets.note: No free pro-C or free pro-p group in either library; the maximal pro-p quotient universal property it would use exists.

targets.target: freeProP p X is pro-p and, for finite X, topologically finitely generated of rank #X; FreeGroup X → freeProP p X is injective (free groups are residually p)
targets.note: No residual p-finiteness of free groups (Mathlib ResiduallyFinite has instances only for finite groups, subgroups and products; no FreeGroup instance), and no topological rank.

targets.target: Rank one: maximalProPQuotient p Ẑ ≅ lim ℤ/p^n ≅ ℤ_p as topological groups; freeProP p (Fin 1) ≅ Multiplicative ℤ_[p]; Sylow characterization in Ẑ
targets.note: Mathlib has only the algebraic half of step 2: compatible families of ring homomorphisms into the ZMod (p^n) lift uniquely to ℤ_[p] (`PadicInt.lift`), and elements are determined by their reductions (`ext_of_toZModPow`). There is no continuity statement for `toZModPow` and no topological or group isomorphism with the inverse limit. Missing: Ẑ, the topological identification, and every group-level step of the chain.

targets.target: Abelian pro-p groups: continuous ℤ_p-exponentiation, topological ℤ_p-module structure, automatic ℤ_p-linearity of continuous homomorphisms; topologically finitely generated ⇒ finitely generated ℤ_p-module
targets.note: Mathlib's only ℤ_p-exponentiation is for topologically unipotent elements of complete normed ℤ_[p]-algebras: `PadicInt.addChar_of_value_at_one` is the continuous character a ↦ (1+r)^a for r with rⁿ → 0, and `continuousAddCharEquiv` classifies continuous characters of ℤ_[p] this way. Nothing gives abelian pro-p groups a ℤ_p-action or a ℤ_p-module structure, and no statement links `IsProP` with `PadicInt`.

targets.target: Structure theorem A ≅ ℤ_p^r × T for topologically finitely generated abelian pro-p A, with uniqueness of r and the elementary divisors
targets.note: The algebraic structure theorem for finitely generated modules over a PID applies to ℤ_[p] (a DVR in Mathlib) but states existence only. Missing: uniqueness of r and of the elementary divisors, the pro-p/topological version, and the passage from abelian pro-p groups to ℤ_p-modules.

targets.target: Coefficient object trivialFp p G (trivial 𝔽_p topological representation) and cohomFp p G n as continuousCohomology
targets.note: The carrier the layer imports exists in every degree for any topological representation, so the 𝔽_p instance is a direct instantiation (the layer notes the ULift universe issue). Only degree 0 of the canonical carrier is computed (ContinuousCohomology.zeroIso).

targets.target: fpPairing and the cup square cupFp : H¹(G,𝔽_p) × H¹(G,𝔽_p) → H²(G,𝔽_p) on the canonical carrier, with graded commutativity
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the (1,1) cup product for any continuous equivariant pairing on its explicit low-degree complex, with graded commutativity and compatibility with restriction and inflation. Missing: ProfiniteCohomology.TopPairing and the cup on Mathlib's canonical continuousCohomology (the explicit and canonical models are identified only in degree 0).

targets.target: presentedProP p X rels; every topologically finitely generated pro-p group has a minimal presentation by a free pro-p group of the same rank, characterized by R ≤ Φ(F)
targets.note: No free or presented pro-p group exists in either library (grep freeProP, "presented pro", IsFreeProfinite returns nothing); only abstract presented groups.

targets.target: Non-vacuity: D₀ = ⟨A,S,Y | A²S⁴(S,Y)⟩ is nontrivial, pro-2 and topologically finitely generated
targets.note: Depends on presentedProP, which does not exist.

targets.target: Continuous extensions 1 → M → E → G → 1 with E profinite and M finite closed normal; morphisms of extensions are isomorphisms
targets.note: Mathlib and Tau Ceti have only abstract (untopologized) group extensions; grep for topological or continuous group extensions finds nothing.

targets.target: Continuous normalized section of E ↠ E/N for a finite normal subgroup N of a profinite group
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves the general case for any closed subgroup of a profinite group (Ribes–Zalesskii 2.2.2), which the layer calls unnecessary but which covers the finite-kernel case; the section sends the identity coset to 1.

targets.target: Continuous 2-cocycle ↔ extension constructions, the bijection of extension classes with H²(G, M) (trivial class = semidirect product), and splitting iff class zero
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the abstract dictionary for G, M : Type: every extension with abelian kernel inducing the action comes from a factor set, two are equivalent iff their H² classes agree, and a factor-set extension splits iff its class vanishes. Missing: the continuous/profinite version with continuous cocycles and sections and the link to the explicit continuous H², and a bundled bijection of extension classes with H².

targets.target: 5.1–5.5: FiniteEmbeddingProblem and IsSolution; HasElementaryAbelianSolutions (from vanishing H²); HasPGroupSolutions by induction; levelProblem compatible systems
targets.note: grep "embedding problem|EmbeddingProblem" returns nothing in either tree.

targets.target: 5.3: lower p-central filtration λ_{k+1}(N) = λ_k(N)^p[λ_k(N), N] of a finite p-group, characteristic, reaching 1 with elementary abelian factors
targets.note: Mathlib has the lower central series and nilpotency of p-groups; no p-central, Jennings or Zassenhaus series in either library (the Frattini description is only its first step).

targets.target: 5.6: projectivity IsProjective p G from p-group solvability by the compactness lemma
targets.note: No projective profinite groups in either library (grep IsProjectiveGroup, "projective profinite", Gruenberg returns nothing).

targets.target: H²(F, M) = 0 for F free pro-p of finite rank and M finite discrete p-primary
targets.note: No free pro-p group, and no vanishing of H² even for abstract free groups.

targets.target: H¹(G, 𝔽_p) ≅ Hom_cont(G, 𝔽_p) ≅ (G/Φ(G))^∨, so dim H¹(G, 𝔽_p) = d(G) for topologically finitely generated pro-p G
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves H¹ ≃ continuous homomorphisms for trivial action on its explicit model. Missing: the identification with the dual of the Frattini quotient, the generator rank, and the transfer to the canonical carrier in degree 1.

targets.target: H² interpretation: transgression H¹(R,𝔽_p)^F ≅ H²(G,𝔽_p) for a minimal presentation via the five-term sequence; r(G) = dim H²(G,𝔽_p) independent of the presentation
targets.note: Only the first terms of inflation-restriction exist (exactness at H¹(G) and res²∘infl² = 0); grep for transgression and five-term finds only docstrings, and relation rank has no hits.

targets.target: Deficiency and one-relator groups: finite relation systems exist iff H² is finite, #S − #R ≥ d − r with equality for minimal presentations
targets.note: grep relation rank, deficiency, one-relator returns nothing relevant.

targets.target: Golod–Shafarevich inequality 4 r(G) > d(G)² for nontrivial finite p-groups
targets.note: grep -i golod and shafarevich returns nothing in either tree.

targets.target: Sanity example d((ℤ/p)^n) = n and r((ℤ/p)^n) = n(n+1)/2
targets.note: No generator or relation rank exists to state it.

duplicates.note: IG.4 also defines weak and proper solutions of finite embedding problems (the 5.1 definitions), for Shafarevich-type realization rather than projectivity.

targets.target: For pro-p G, testing cd_p on the single module 𝔽_p (cd_p_le_iff_elementaryAbelian_of_isProP), with cd_p imported from ProfiniteCohomology
targets.note: Neither library defines cohomological dimension (grep "cohomological dimension|cohomologicalDimension|cd_p" finds only gcd lemmas).

targets.target: Trivial-filtration theorem: a nonzero finite discrete p-primary module over a pro-p group has nonzero invariants, hence a G-stable filtration with trivial one-dimensional factors, and additive invariants equal length times the value at 𝔽_p
targets.note: Mathlib supplies the finite input (a p-group acting on a finite set of order divisible by p with a fixed point has another fixed point). Missing: the module statement for pro-p groups acting through a finite quotient, the filtration and the length formula.

targets.target: Dévissage from elementary abelian to all finite p-primary modules, and vanishing of H² for all such modules implying vanishing in all degrees ≥ 2 by dimension shifting through Coind_1^G
targets.note: All-degree tools exist, but not the continuous ones this layer needs. Mathlib's `continuousCohomology n` is defined in every degree, Tau Ceti adds an all-degree finite-quotient system (`finiteQuotientSystem`, without its colimit comparison), and Mathlib's Shapiro isomorphism `groupCohomology.coindIso` holds in every degree for abstract groups. For continuous cohomology Tau Ceti has coinduced discrete modules and Shapiro only in degrees 0 and 1 (closed subgroups, profinite G), and its long exact sequence stops at H². There is no acyclicity of Coind_1, no dimension shifting and no dévissage.

targets.target: Free pro-p ⇒ cd_p ≤ 1, and Serre: cd_p G ≤ 1 ⇒ G free pro-p for topologically finitely generated G
targets.note: No free pro-p groups and no cohomological dimension.

targets.target: cd_p U = cd_p G for U open in pro-p G with cd_p G < ∞
targets.note: Needs all-degree Shapiro and cd_p, neither of which exists.

targets.target: Sylow equality cd_p G = cd_p G_p, including the colimit description of the cohomology of a closed subgroup over open subgroups containing it
targets.note: Available ingredients: cor∘res = [G:U] in degrees 0–2 for open U of finite index (explicit model) and profinite Sylow existence; no cd_p and no closed-subgroup colimit description.

targets.target: Two-term Euler formula finrank H⁰(U) − finrank H¹(U) = [G:U](finrank H⁰(G) − finrank H¹(G)) for t.f.g. pro-p G with cd_p ≤ 1
targets.note: No group-cohomology Euler characteristic in either library.

targets.target: Pro-p Nielsen–Schreier: an open subgroup of index m in a free pro-p group of rank n ≥ 1 is free pro-p of rank 1 + m(n − 1)
targets.note: Only the abstract Nielsen–Schreier theorem (subgroups of free groups are free) exists, without the index formula.

targets.target: IsDemushkin p G (pro-p, dim H¹ finite, dim H² = 1, nondegenerate cup pairing) with derived topological finite generation, demushkinRank, one-relator presentation and invariance under isomorphism
targets.note: grep -i demu[sš]kin, labute returns nothing in either tree.

targets.target: First examples: ℤ/2 is the unique finite and the unique rank-1 Demushkin group at p = 2; free pro-p groups are not Demushkin; ℤ_p × ℤ_p is Demushkin with q = 0; no rank-1 Demushkin group for odd p
targets.note: No Demushkin predicate.

targets.target: Abelianization structure G^ab ≅ ℤ_p^{n−1} × ℤ_p/qℤ_p, well-definedness of demushkinQ, and D₀^ab ≅ ℤ₂² × ℤ/2
targets.note: Mathlib defines the topological abelianization G ⧸ closure[G,G] with its CommGroup instance only; no structure theorem, and the Layer 4 abelian pro-p structure theorem it relies on is missing.

targets.target: Prescription property (Labute Prop. 6): equivalence of surjectivity of H¹(G, I(χ)/p^i) → H¹(G, I(χ)/p), vanishing connecting maps, and compatible crossed homomorphisms with prescribed values
targets.note: No such statements in either library.

targets.target: Canonical character: a Demushkin group has a unique continuous χ : G → ℤ_pˣ with the prescription property; closed image, isomorphism invariance, Im χ = 1 + qℤ_p for q ≠ 2
targets.note: Only the arithmetic cyclotomic character exists; no abstract orientation of a pro-p group.

targets.target: Closed subgroups of ℤ₂ˣ (U^(f), V^(f), U^[f]) with exhaustiveness, procyclicity and indices; ℤ_pˣ ≅ μ_{p−1} × (1 + pℤ_p) and the p-adic logarithm 1 + pℤ_p ≅ pℤ_p for odd p; closed subgroups of 1 + pℤ_p
targets.note: Mathlib has the ideals of ℤ_p and cyclicity of (ℤ/p^n)ˣ; Tau Ceti has Teichmüller lifts and unit filtrations for general nonarchimedean local fields. No p-adic logarithm (grep padicLog, Padic.log finds nothing), no decomposition of ℤ_pˣ, no classification of its closed subgroups.

targets.target: Dimension two: an infinite Demushkin group has cd_p G = 2
targets.note: No cd_p and no Demushkin groups.

targets.target: Duality package: trace isomorphism H²(G,𝔽_p) ≅ 𝔽_p, perfect cup pairings on the I(χ)/p^i system, naturality with restriction and corestriction, role of χ
targets.note: No duality for profinite group cohomology in either library (perfect-pairing hits are linear algebra only).

targets.target: Three-term Euler formula for t.f.g. pro-p G with cd_p ≤ 2 and finite H⁰, H¹, H²
targets.note: No group-cohomology Euler characteristic.

targets.target: Open-subgroup theorem: U open in infinite Demushkin G is Demushkin with n(U) − 2 = [G:U](n(G) − 2) and χ_U = χ_G|_U
targets.note: No Demushkin groups.

targets.target: Recognition criteria (NSW 3.9.15): for one-relator t.f.g. pro-p G with n(G) > 1, Demushkin iff cd_p = 2 with dim H²(N) = 1, iff cd_p = 2 with the rank formula for open normal N
targets.note: No Demushkin groups or cd_p.

duplicates.note: LocalFieldsRamification Layer 1 proves 𝒪[K]ˣ ≃ μ_{q−1} × U(K,1) and the deep-unit logarithm U(K,i) ≅ 𝓂[K]^i for (p−1)i > e over finite K/ℚ_p; at K = ℚ_p these are the decomposition ℤ_pˣ ≅ μ_{p−1} × (1 + pℤ_p) and the isomorphisms 1 + pℤ_p ≅ pℤ_p (p odd) and 1 + 4ℤ₂ ≅ 4ℤ₂ that T5 states.

targets.target: Lower p-series λ_k = pLowerCentralSeries p G (closed, normal, characteristic, λ_{k+1} ≤ λ_k) and gradedPiece gr_k = λ_k/λ_{k+1} as an 𝔽_p-vector space; finite under topological finite generation
targets.note: Only the first step exists: λ_1 = Φ(G) = closure(G^p[G,G]) with elementary abelian quotient gr_0. The series itself, the higher graded pieces and their finiteness are absent.

targets.target: gradedBracket gr_j × gr_k → gr_{j+k+1} and gradedPow gr_k → gr_{k+1} with bilinearity, alternation, Jacobi, additivity except in degree 0 at p = 2, the dyadic identities and naturality (Labute Props. 1–2)
targets.note: No restricted or mixed Lie algebra of a pro-p group and no Hall–Petrescu formula (grep returns nothing); Mathlib has the Hall–Witt identity.

targets.target: Openness and cofinality of λ_k in t.f.g. pro-p groups, G ≅ lim G/λ_k, f(λ_k(G)) ≤ λ_k(H) with equality for surjections, interleaving with the iterated Frattini series
targets.note: Tau Ceti has an abstract cofinal sequence of open normal subgroups and the k = 1 surjectivity statement; nothing for the lower p-series.

targets.target: Basis-modification maps δ_j with linearity for j ≥ 2 and the polarization identity at j = 1, tails T_j, and the (A : A²) parameters of normal forms
targets.note: No lower p-series or relator calculus in either library.

targets.target: IsFiniteContinuousQuotient G Q via surjections with open kernel, with invariance under isomorphism
targets.note: No such predicate in either tree.

targets.target: Finite-quotient determinacy: t.f.g. G and H with the same continuous finite quotients admit surjections both ways and are isomorphic (no finite-generation hypothesis on H); corollary for profinite completions of f.g. abstract groups
targets.note: The Hopf property and finiteness of open subgroups of each index (the two inputs) are in Tau Ceti; grep "profinitely|same finite quotients|profinite rigidity" returns nothing.

targets.target: Levelwise comparison schema: finite nonempty level data with surjective bonding maps and compatible realizations yield a continuous surjection G ↠ H inducing them, plus the two-sided corollary
targets.note: Mathlib has nonemptiness of inverse limits of nonempty finite sets (without needing surjective bonding maps); the schema assembling group homomorphisms along the lower p-series does not exist.

targets.target: Bilinear forms over 𝔽_p: left and right radicals, left and right nondegeneracy agreeing in finite dimension, transport and equivalence of forms
targets.note: Tau Ceti names the left and right radicals (`TauCeti.leftRadical` is `b.ker`, `rightRadical` is `b.flip.ker`) for any sesquilinear map over a commutative ring, with `separatingLeft_iff_leftRadical_eq_bot` and its right analogue. In Mathlib, one-sided nondegeneracy implies nondegeneracy for finite free modules over a domain (`Nondegenerate.ofSeparatingLeft`/`ofSeparatingRight`, `nondegenerate_iff_ker_eq_bot`), `congr` transports forms along linear equivalences, and `LinearMap.BilinForm.Equivalent` is the existence of an isometry equivalence, with nondegeneracy transported by `Nondegenerate.congr`.

targets.target: Alternating implies skew-symmetric in every characteristic; at p = 2 skew-symmetric equals symmetric and x ↦ b(x,x) is semilinear; for odd p symmetric and alternating forces zero
targets.note: Alternating ⇒ skew-symmetric is in Mathlib over any commutative ring, and Tau Ceti proves that a symmetric alternating form is zero whenever 2 is left-regular (`TauCeti.BilinForm.eq_zero_of_isSymm_of_isAlt`), which covers odd p. Only the characteristic-2 comparisons are not stated: skew-symmetric equals symmetric, and x ↦ b(x,x) is additive and semilinear.

targets.target: Symplectic normal form: a nondegenerate alternating form over any field (including characteristic 2) has a basis with blocks [[0,1],[−1,0]], so the dimension is even
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves even dimension only for real symplectic vector spaces; no symplectic basis theorem over a general field (grep symplectic basis, exists_symplectic finds only Darboux-type analysis).

targets.target: Characteristic 2: a nondegenerate symmetric non-alternating form over 𝔽₂ has an orthonormal (identity-matrix) basis, completing the classification of nondegenerate symmetric bilinear forms over 𝔽₂; the combined change-of-basis theorem
targets.note: Mathlib diagonalizes symmetric forms only when 2 is invertible, so it does not apply over 𝔽₂.

targets.target: From the cup matrix to the relator: coefficients of r̄ in gr_1(F) ≅ Λ²(𝔽_p^n) ⊕ 𝔽_p^n are the cup-matrix entries, transforming by B ↦ PᵀBP (Labute Prop. 3)
targets.note: No lower p-series or free pro-p groups.

targets.target: completedGroupAlgebra p Γ = lim_U ℤ_p[Γ/U] as a compact totally disconnected topological ℤ_p-algebra, commutative for abelian Γ, with projections, of : Γ →* Λˣ and functoriality
targets.note: No completed group algebra or Iwasawa algebra in either tree; Mathlib only identifies ℤ_p-valued measures on ℤ_p with ℤ_[p]⟦X⟧ as a linear equivalence (no convolution ring structure).

targets.target: IsCompactModule with separatedness, surjective transitions, quotient stability and compactModule_limit_surjective
targets.note: No compact modules over completed group algebras.

targets.target: Power-series coordinate ℤ_p[[T]] ≅ completedGroupAlgebra p Γ for Γ ≅ ℤ_p, generator dependence T ↦ (1+T)^u − 1, and the filtration statement
targets.note: The Amice transform is the linear shadow of this isomorphism; the algebra isomorphism is missing. Contrary to the README (which says PowerSeries carries no topology at its pin), Mathlib at this baseline has the scoped coefficientwise topology PowerSeries.WithPiTopology, which for compact ℤ_p is the (p,T)-adic topology.

targets.target: Evaluation ψ ↦ ψ(c) : ℤ_p[[T]] → ℤ_p for v_p(c) ≥ 1 as a ℤ_p-algebra homomorphism
targets.note: Mathlib evaluates power series at topologically nilpotent elements of complete linearly topologized rings (`eval₂`, `aeval`). For ℤ_[p] both inputs are one step away: an element divisible by p has norm < 1, so its powers tend to 0 (`PadicInt.norm_lt_one_iff_dvd`, `tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_norm_lt_one`), which is `HasEval`; `IsLinearTopology ℤ_[p] ℤ_[p]` is not an instance but follows from `Ideal.isLinearTopology` and Tau Ceti's proof that the topology of ℤ_[p] is (p)-adic. The ℤ_p evaluation homomorphism itself is not stated.

targets.target: Division criterion (T − c) ∣ ψ in ℤ_p[[T]] iff ψ(c) = 0, for v_p(c) ≥ 1
targets.note: Mathlib has Weierstrass division and preparation over complete local rings, and ℤ_[p] has the required IsAdicComplete maximal-ideal instance, so division by T − c with remainder a constant is available; the identification of the remainder with ψ(c), and hence the criterion, is not stated.

targets.target: Dyadic branch Γ ≅ C₂ × ℤ₂: completedGroupAlgebra 2 Γ ≅ ℤ₂[C₂][[T]], eigenspace splitting after inverting 2, and ℤ₂[C₂] has only the idempotents 0 and 1
targets.note: No completed group algebras; no statement about idempotents of ℤ₂[C₂].

targets.target: Labute's relation module E = ker χ/(ker χ, ker χ) with conjugation action, Λ-scalar action and module laws, relationModuleToLabuteE and the relator class
targets.note: grep "relation module", labute returns nothing.

targets.note: Nothing present.

EnhancedDerivedSheaves.summary: Nothing homotopy-coherent in this roadmap exists: neither library has mapping spaces of quasicategories or an API for their equivalences, dg nerves, stable ∞-categories, straightening, presentable ∞-categories, hypercover descent, limits of Postnikov towers or left completion, derived completion, ∞-operads, E∞-algebras, animated rings or spectra. Mathlib supplies the named starting points and their 1-categorical shadows: quasicategories with inner fibrations, nerves, quasicategorical internal homs and the homotopy 2-category of quasicategories, Dold–Kan and the simplicial nerve, sheaves of modules as a Grothendieck abelian category with enough injectives, K-injective complexes, the unbounded derived category with t-structures, truncation towers and detection of isomorphisms by cohomology, repleteness of coherent and light condensed topoi, and 1-categorical Kan extensions, adjoint functor theorems, orthogonal reflections, mates, Karoubi and Ind-completions, sifted colimits and the naive cotangent complex; Tau Ceti adds the DG enrichment of complexes. Everything the layers actually own (the enhancement, its sheaf-theoretic operations, descent, coherent adjoints, derived completion of sheaves, monoidal and animated structures, the positive-characteristic E∞ comparison and the spectra comparison) remains to be built; apart from that comparison, E5:cotangent-export re-exports DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0.

targets.target: Equivalence, mapping-space, functor and natural-transformation theory for quasicategories, with extended universe support
targets.note: E0 reuses Mathlib's quasicategories, inner fibrations and nerve API (`SSet.Quasicategory`, `SSet.InnerFibration`, `SSet.quasicategory_iff_innerFibration`, `CategoryTheory.Nerve.quasicategory`), which the layer names as inputs. Mathlib also proves that the internal hom Fun(A,X) into a quasicategory is a quasicategory (anonymous instance at PushoutProduct.lean:156, via the cited pullback-hom lemma), has the homotopy-category functor, and has the homotopy 2-category of quasicategories (`SSet.QCat.bicategory`, `SSet.QCat.strictBicategory`), in which equivalences can be expressed through `Bicategory.Equivalence`. Missing: an API for equivalences of quasicategories, the Joyal model structure, mapping spaces, and the extended universe support (Quasicategory/Basic.lean records the universe restriction as a TODO).

targets.target: dg nerve of a DG category via truncation and Dold–Kan of mapping complexes, with coherent composition and mapping-space and homotopy-category descriptions
targets.note: grep "dg nerve" returns nothing; the homotopy coherent (simplicial) nerve, Dold–Kan and the DG enrichment of complexes are the available inputs.

targets.target: Equivalences, slices, limits and colimits in quasicategories with mapping-space universal properties
targets.note: No joins or slices of simplicial sets and no (co)limits in quasicategories in either library.

targets.target: Stable ∞-category API: zero objects, fibres and cofibres, suspension, exact functors, triangulated homotopy categories, and comparison of shifts and cone signs with the cochain-complex convention
targets.note: Only 1-categorical triangulated categories and the pretriangulated homotopy category of complexes exist; grep "stable ∞" returns nothing.

targets.target: coCartesian fibrations and sections over Δ, products with intervals and refinement diagrams; restricted straightening/unstraightening with fibrewise evaluation and naturality
targets.note: Mathlib has 1-categorical cocartesian morphisms and the Grothendieck construction of a pseudofunctor, but no cocartesian fibrations of simplicial sets and no straightening (grep straighten finds only Young tableaux).

targets.target: Sheaves of modules on a small site as a Grothendieck abelian category with enough injectives
targets.note: SheafOfModules is over a sheaf of rings (more general than a constant commutative coefficient ring); its IsGrothendieckAbelian instance is an anonymous public instance in Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Abelian/GrothendieckAxioms/SheafOfModules.lean for small sites.

targets.target: The unbounded dg category of complexes of sheaves of modules
targets.note: Tau Ceti enriches cochain complexes in any R-linear preadditive category over complexes of R-modules; it is not instantiated for sheaves of modules.

targets.target: Functorial K-injective and K-flat replacements for unbounded complexes in Grothendieck abelian categories, with size bounds
targets.note: K-injective complexes are defined and bounded-below complexes have injective replacements; existence of unbounded K-injective replacements and all K-flat theory are missing (grep K-flat returns nothing).

targets.target: Dg nerve of the K-injective model with homotopy category the unbounded derived category, mapping spaces from derived Hom, stability
targets.note: Mathlib has the unbounded derived category of an abelian category as a 1-categorical localization, triangulated; no ∞-categorical model.

targets.target: Filtered homotopy colimits, generating sets, accessible localization at quasi-isomorphisms and presentability of the enhanced derived category
targets.note: Mathlib has 1-categorical locally presentable categories (with instances only for types and presheaves); nothing ∞-categorical, and no proof that Grothendieck abelian categories are locally presentable.

targets.target: Derived tensor product from the K-flat model transferred through the comparison
targets.note: grep "derived tensor" returns nothing in either tree.

targets.target: Enhanced pullback/pushforward adjunction for morphisms of sites and ringed topoi with derived tensor, agreeing with exact sheaf pullback at constant coefficients
targets.note: Only the underived pullback–pushforward adjunction for sheaves of modules exists.

targets.target: Symmetric monoidal coherence, derived internal Hom, change of coefficients, compatibility with ordinary derived functors, detection of equivalences by quasi-isomorphisms and cohomology sheaves
targets.note: The 1-categorical detection statements exist: a morphism of D(A) is an isomorphism iff it induces isomorphisms on all cohomology objects (`DerivedCategory.isIso_iff`; cohomology sheaves when A is a sheaf category), and a morphism of complexes becomes an isomorphism in D(A) iff it is a quasi-isomorphism (`DerivedCategory.isIso_Q_map_iff_quasiIso`). Change of coefficients exists underived (`SheafOfModules.restrictScalars`), and Mathlib has derived functors of exact functors and total derived functors as Kan extensions. Missing: the enhanced versions, symmetric monoidal coherence, derived internal Hom and any monoidal structure on derived categories of sheaves.

duplicates.note: D0 (a declared prerequisite of E1) also builds sheaves of modules with exact sheafification and enough injectives, the ordinary input E1 starts from; both are already in Mathlib.
S.1 also constructs complexes of sheaves of modules with quasi-isomorphisms and chooses an enhanced model, overlapping the enhancement of complexes of module sheaves built here.

targets.target: Truncations and Postnikov towers with enhanced inverse limits; the left completion of a derived category with its universal comparison and criteria for an equivalence
targets.note: Mathlib has t-structures, truncation functors, the canonical t-structure on D(A) and the Postnikov tower of a t-structure as a functor (`TStructure.eTruncGE : EInt ⥤ C ⥤ C`, with `eTruncLT`), all 1-categorical. Limits of the tower (ordinary or enhanced), their convergence and the left completion with its universal comparison are absent (grep postnikov, 'left complet' finds nothing).

targets.target: Replete-topos results (Bhatt–Scholze §3): exactness of inverse limits of surjections, convergence of derived Postnikov towers, unbounded cohomological descent, the bounded-below comparison and the finite cohomological dimension criterion
targets.note: Mathlib proves the first replete-topos property for particular topoi: a sequential limit of epimorphisms of sheaves is epimorphic for the coherent topology on a preregular finitary extensive category whose sequential limits preserve effective epimorphisms (`coherentTopology.epi_π_app_zero_of_epi`), and for light condensed modules (`LightCondensed.epi_π_app_zero_of_epi`, with `CountableAB4Star (LightCondMod R)`). There is no general notion of a replete topos, and convergence of derived Postnikov towers, unbounded cohomological descent, the bounded-below comparison and the finite cohomological dimension criterion are absent. Mathlib has the pro-étale site of a scheme.

targets.target: Simplicial sites, cartesian complexes, hypercovers and totalizations; enhanced equivalence of sheaves with cartesian objects on a hypercover, cofinality and independence of the hypercover
targets.note: Only 1-hypercovers (for the sheaf condition) and Čech nerves exist; no n-hypercovers, simplicial sites or cohomological descent.

targets.target: Enhanced category of a diagram of ringed topoi with coherent pullback functors (Liu–Zheng §2)
targets.note: Nothing present.

targets.target: Left Kan extension along a full inclusion with pointwise formula via slices, uniqueness and compatibility with coCartesian diagrams (HTT §4.3.2)
targets.note: Mathlib has pointwise Kan extensions, their uniqueness and the fully faithful case for ordinary categories; nothing for quasicategories or coCartesian diagrams.

targets.target: Cofinality for restricting from a total diagram to a fibre, and preservation of coCartesian edges by fibrewise transformations
targets.note: No coCartesian fibrations of simplicial sets.

targets.target: Accessible localizations and reflective/coreflective subcategories of presentable categories
targets.note: Mathlib constructs the reflection onto W-local objects for small W with presentable (co)domains in locally presentable 1-categories; no ∞-categorical version.

targets.target: Adjoint functor theorem for colimit-preserving functors between presentable categories producing the right adjoint, enhanced adjunction uniqueness, cutoffs for large sites
targets.note: The general and special adjoint functor theorems exist for ordinary categories; the presentable ∞-categorical form and its coherence are missing.

targets.target: An exact functor between stable cocomplete categories preserving coproducts preserves all small colimits
targets.note: No statement for triangulated or stable categories (grep Brown representability, compactly generated triangulated returns nothing).

targets.target: Mates, Beck–Chevalley transformations and identity/composition/pasting coherence for (enhanced) adjunctions
targets.note: Mathlib has the 1-categorical (and bicategorical) mate correspondence with pasting laws; nothing for adjunctions of ∞-categories.

targets.target: Derived I-adic completion re-exported from DD.1: Koszul/localization completeness for finitely generated ideals, adjunction, generator independence, reduction conservativity, completed tensors and inverse-limit comparisons
targets.note: Only classical adic completion and regular sequences exist; grep "derived complet", Koszul complex and lim¹ return nothing (the Koszul complex is a Mathlib TODO).

targets.target: Enhanced inverse limit of the categories with coefficients Λ/I^n and the reconstruction theorem under completeness and regular-sequence hypotheses, including nonnoetherian rings
targets.note: Nothing present.

targets.target: Completed tensor products and colimits in the sheaf setting; reduction and finite-level coefficient change commuting with the eligible operations, dévissage from I to I^n
targets.note: Nothing present.

duplicates.note: DD.1 owns the generic derived completion (Koszul model, adjunction, generator independence, conservativity, completed tensors, inverse-limit comparisons) that E4 re-exports before extending it to sheaves.
P7 also constructs derived completion and derived tensor products, for perfect complexes over complete Noetherian local rings.

targets.target: Symmetric monoidal ∞-categories via coCartesian fibrations over finite pointed sets, Segal conditions, ∞-operads, operadic algebras, modules and monoidal functors with coherent universal properties
targets.note: Only strict Segal simplicial sets and 1-categorical symmetric monoidal categories exist; grep operad, "Gamma space", E∞ finds nothing (operad only in a bibliography).

targets.target: Exact, idempotent-complete stable ∞-categories and the Karoubi envelope
targets.note: The 1-categorical Karoubi envelope with its universal property exists; no stable ∞-categories and no triangulated or stable structure on idempotent completions.

targets.target: Ind-completion, compact-object comparison and extension of exact functors to colimit-preserving functors, with tensor/Ind and module/base-change compatibilities under compact generation
targets.note: Mathlib has 1-categorical Ind-objects and finitely presentable objects; the ∞-categorical Ind-completion, the extension of exact functors and the compact-generation compatibilities are missing.

targets.target: Finite and profinite coherent group actions on categories, homotopy fixed points and equivariant functor categories with continuity through finite quotients
targets.note: grep "homotopy fixed" and equivariantization returns nothing; only monoidal actions and shift structures exist.

targets.target: Animated commutative algebras from simplicial commutative rings, polynomial resolutions, sifted left Kan extensions and tensor pushouts
targets.note: grep animated and "simplicial commutative ring" return nothing; Mathlib has sifted categories (sifted colimits commute with finite products) and polynomial presentations of algebras.

targets.target: Cotangent complex with derivation characterization, transitivity and base change, derived exterior powers and Tor-amplitude tests (the DD.0 interface), and comparison with E∞-algebras in positive characteristic in proved ranges
targets.note: Mathlib has the naive (two-term) cotangent complex, its H¹ and the Jacobi–Zariski sequence; the full derived cotangent complex, derived exterior powers, Tor amplitude and E∞ comparisons are missing.

targets.target: Comparison of concrete spectra and spectral module categories with the abstract stable monoidal construction: exact tensor, Eilenberg–MacLane and coherent action comparisons
targets.note: Neither library has spectra (grep prespectrum, orthogonal/symmetric spectrum returns nothing); Tau Ceti has only K(G,1) spaces.

targets.target: Acceptance tests: cotangent module of a polynomial algebra, two-term cotangent complex of a regular quotient, a nonregular quotient with higher homology, Ind-envelope of perfect modules, coherent action with higher group cohomology in its invariants
targets.note: Kähler differentials of polynomial algebras are free on the dx_i and the naive two-term cotangent complex exists; the derived computations, the Ind-envelope and the coherent action test are missing.

duplicates.note: DD.0 constructs the cotangent complex, derived exterior powers and Tor-amplitude criteria that E5 re-exports.

targets.target: Symmetric monoidal ∞-categories via coCartesian fibrations over finite pointed sets, Segal conditions, ∞-operads, operadic algebras, modules and monoidal functors with coherent universal properties
targets.note: Only strict Segal simplicial sets and 1-categorical symmetric monoidal categories exist; grep operad, "Gamma space", E∞ finds nothing (operad only in a bibliography).

targets.target: Exact, idempotent-complete stable ∞-categories and the Karoubi envelope
targets.note: The 1-categorical Karoubi envelope with its universal property exists; no stable ∞-categories and no triangulated or stable structure on idempotent completions.

targets.target: Animated commutative algebras from simplicial commutative rings, polynomial resolutions, sifted left Kan extensions and tensor pushouts
targets.note: grep animated and "simplicial commutative ring" return nothing; Mathlib has sifted categories (sifted colimits commute with finite products) and polynomial presentations of algebras.

targets.target: Cotangent complex with derivation characterization, transitivity and base change, derived exterior powers and Tor-amplitude tests (the DD.0 interface), and comparison with E∞-algebras in positive characteristic in proved ranges
targets.note: The DD.0 interface is partial in Mathlib: the naive (two-term) cotangent complex, its H¹ and the Jacobi–Zariski sequence exist; the full derived cotangent complex, derived exterior powers and Tor amplitude are missing, and DD.0 owns them. The positive-characteristic comparison with E∞-algebras in proved ranges is stated only in this stage (DD.0 does not mention E∞-algebras) and is absent: neither library has E∞-algebras.

targets.target: Ind-completion, compact-object comparison and extension of exact functors to colimit-preserving functors, with tensor/Ind and module/base-change compatibilities under compact generation
targets.note: Mathlib has 1-categorical Ind-objects and finitely presentable objects; the ∞-categorical Ind-completion, the extension of exact functors and the compact-generation compatibilities are missing.

targets.target: Finite and profinite coherent group actions on categories, homotopy fixed points and equivariant functor categories with continuity through finite quotients
targets.note: grep "homotopy fixed" and equivariantization returns nothing; only monoidal actions and shift structures exist.

targets.target: Algebra and module categories and the Eilenberg–MacLane comparison once concrete spectra exist
targets.note: The layer defers this to 'a later branch once the concrete spectra are available', which is E5:spectra-comparison (its T0 covers the same comparison). Neither library has spectra.

targets.target: Comparison of concrete spectra and spectral module categories with the abstract stable monoidal construction: exact tensor, Eilenberg–MacLane and coherent action comparisons
targets.note: Neither library has spectra (grep prespectrum, orthogonal/symmetric spectrum returns nothing); Tau Ceti has only K(G,1) spaces.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/DGAInfinity.summary: Tau Ceti already has most of Layer 0 and the algebra-level core of Layers 1–3, beyond what its 1 September STATUS.md reports: internal gradings with shifts, tensor products, opposites and direct sums; signed one-slot substitution and suspension; reduced and coaugmented tensor coalgebras with the coderivation/Taylor equivalence; the Koszul braiding and the linear Hom-complex enrichment of complexes; the Stasheff identities with b² = 0 ⇔ Stasheff; unital and augmented DG algebras with tensor products, cohomology algebras and left/right DG modules; nonunital A∞ algebras with strict, cohomological and augmented units, strict morphisms and the reduced algebra on the augmentation ideal, whose bar differential is the reduced bar construction in pieces; and normalization of contractions. Mathlib contributes general enriched categories, signed shifts of Hom complexes, the triangulated thick closure and Verdier localization, and Tau Ceti's Grothendieck-group library supplies the triangulated K₀, Ext-Euler pairing and numerical quotients that Layer 10 would specialize. Genuinely missing: DG categories as a theory (H⁰, quasi-equivalences), all bimodules, A∞ morphisms beyond strict ones, A∞ categories and modules, homological transfer and Kadeishvili, the bar construction as a DG coalgebra, cobar, twisting cochains and Maurer–Cartan twisting, derived module categories and envelopes, derived Morita theory, DG quotients, Hochschild theory and Massey products, smooth/proper and Calabi–Yau structures, K₀(Perf) Euler theory, and Koszul duality.

targets.target: Internal ℤ-gradings (direct-sum decompositions of a total module) with homogeneous induction, degreewise extensionality, shifts, tensor products, opposites and direct sums
targets.note: Homogeneous induction comes from the DirectSum.Decomposition instance (Mathlib DirectSum.Decomposition.inductionOn) and InternalGrading.linearMap_ext.

targets.target: Equivalence between the internal-grading presentation and Mathlib graded objects
targets.note: Conversions in both directions with object-level isomorphisms exist; there is no functor or equivalence of categories between the two presentations.

targets.target: Duals of graded modules under finite-projectivity hypotheses, with their tensor-product identifications
targets.note: A graded dual exists for gradings with finitely many nonzero pieces; the finite-projective hypotheses and the tensor/dual identifications are not built (the file header says so).

targets.target: Homogeneous multilinear maps with a degree, and substitution of a degree-q operation after the first r inputs with the exact Koszul sign
targets.note: signedOneSlot and koszulSign live in the root MultilinearMap namespace; the prefix degrees are passed explicitly.

targets.target: Brace operations with several insertions, and dependent multilinear maps along composable paths in a graded quiver with transport along linear equivalences
targets.note: grep "graded quiver|GradedQuiver" returns nothing, and "brace" only a citation; only one-slot substitution exists.

targets.target: Reduced and coaugmented tensor coalgebras with deconcatenation, conilpotence filtration, coderivations and the equivalence of degree-one (Koszul-signed) coderivations with Taylor components
targets.note: Plain coderivEquivTaylor (Coderivation.lean:489) accompanies the signed version; the coaugmented version is a Mathlib Coalgebra.

targets.target: Completed tensor coalgebras as products over tensor length, distinguished from the direct-sum conilpotent coalgebra
targets.note: grep CompletedTensor/"completed tensor" returns nothing in either tree.

targets.target: Symmetric monoidal structure on CochainComplex (ModuleCat k) ℤ: braiding with the Koszul sign, hexagons and symmetry on Mathlib monoidal structure
targets.note: Built on Mathlib HomologicalComplex.monoidalCategory, as the layer requires.

targets.target: k-linear Hom complex with signed differential, closed composition and enrichment of complexes over complexes of k-modules, compared with Mathlib CochainComplex.HomComplex
targets.note: For an R-linear preadditive category; the enriched composition is the Koszul braiding followed by Keller composition.

targets.target: Suspension/unsuspension, the general Stasheff component formula and the arity 1–4 equations, and b² = 0 iff all Stasheff identities
targets.note: Arity 1–4 forms stasheffSum_one…four (Stasheff.lean:582–614); the Stasheff.lean header still says the b² link is owed, but it is proved in Coderivation.lean. The roadmap STATUS.md (1 September) also lists it as missing. The A∞ sign bookkeeping goes through Tau Ceti helpers over Mathlib's Int.negOnePow (`negOnePowCast`, `suspExp`, `koszulSign`), not through Mathlib's `ComplexShape.TensorSigns`, which the layer names as the accepted endpoint; the mathematics is present, but that instruction is not followed.

targets.target: Unital DG algebras on internally graded algebras with morphisms, tensor products, cycles/boundaries, the graded cohomology algebra, and the zero-differential constructor
targets.note: Over a commutative ring; the cohomology carries a GradedAlgebra instance and DGAlgHom.cohomologyMap gives functoriality. Mathlib has no DG algebras.

targets.note: With the splitting splitLinearEquiv.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GrothendieckEuler.summary: Tau Ceti already implements most of this roadmap, well beyond its 1 September STATUS.md: Bühler exact structures with conflation-exact functors, the presented-K₀ engine with equivalence invariance across smallness universes, split/exact/abelian/triangulated K₀ with graded ℤ-actions, the projective resolution theorem with horseshoe and Schanuel, the Cartan map of any ring and its inverse under finite projective resolutions, the simple basis of G₀ and the Hom-multiplicity formula, Euler–Poincaré for invariants on an abelian category, Euler-admissible Ext-Euler pairings with graded and sesquilinear q-Euler versions over LaurentK0, and left/right numerical quotients with the Ext-Euler specialization. Genuinely missing are admissible morphisms and the converse bicartesian criteria, a named choice-independence comparison with its naturality, product compatibility of K₀, bounded homotopy/derived-category comparisons, Euler–Poincaré on exact subcategories, general resolving subcategories and the common-refinement resolution theorem, graded and linear (Koszul) resolutions, the Cartan matrix with projective bases, pairing perfectness and unimodularity, Ext-Euler naturality and the quiver comparison, and the q = ±1 specializations and forget-the-grading comparison.

targets.target: Kernel–cokernel pairs with their kernel and cokernel universal properties, the bridge to Mathlib limit/colimit witnesses, and isomorphisms of pairs
targets.note: Mathlib has no IsKernel/IsCokernel types, so the bridge is to IsLimit of the kernel fork and IsColimit of the cokernel cofork; isomorphisms of conflations are ladders of three isomorphisms.

targets.target: ExactStructure: an isomorphism-closed class of kernel–cokernel pairs with Bühler E0/E0op, E1/E1op, E2/E2op, where E2 produces genuine pushouts of inflations and E2op genuine pullbacks of deflations
targets.note: The axioms are recorded as MorphismProperty instances and property-specific pushout/pullback classes, so no ambient pushouts or pullbacks are assumed. Mathlib has no exact-category notion.

targets.target: Standard consequences: split sequences are conflations, direct sums of conflations are conflations, isomorphisms are inflations and deflations
targets.note: Isomorphisms being inflations and deflations follows from the identity axiom and isomorphism closure, which are packaged as RespectsIso and ContainsIdentities instances rather than a named lemma.

targets.target: Bicartesian characterization of pushouts along inflations and pullbacks along deflations (Bühler Prop. 2.12)
targets.note: Only the forward implications are proved (a pushout along an inflation gives a conflation and a bicartesian square, dually for pullbacks); the converse directions of the equivalence are missing.

targets.target: Inflations, deflations, admissible morphisms, maps and isomorphisms of conflations
targets.note: Admissible morphisms (a deflation followed by an inflation) are not defined; grep finds them only in docstrings.

targets.target: The opposite exact structure, with inflations and deflations exchanged
targets.note: Dual statements elsewhere (injectives, pullbacks) are derived through this structure.

targets.target: Conflation-exact functors: identity, composition, natural-isomorphism invariance, reflection of conflations, transfer of an exact structure along an equivalence
targets.note: Transport comes with isConflationExact_functor_transport and reflectsConflations_functor_transport.

targets.target: Exact equivalences as a notion, and preservation of admissible pushouts and pullbacks by conflation-exact functors
targets.note: Exact equivalences are used unbundled: `ExactK0.mapEquiv` takes an equivalence whose two functors are conflation-exact (its docstring's definition of an exact equivalence), and `isConflationExact_inverse_iff_reflectsConflations` characterizes the condition on the inverse; only the graded `GradedExactEquiv` is bundled as a structure. No lemma says that a conflation-exact functor preserves pushouts along inflations or pullbacks along deflations.

targets.target: For abelian categories with canonical exact structures, conflation-exact iff preserving finite limits and colimits (comparison with Mathlib)
targets.note: Stated for additive functors between abelian categories, via Mathlib exact_tfae.

targets.target: Split exact structure on an additive category, canonical exact structure on an abelian category, induced structure on an extension-closed full additive subcategory with exact reflecting inclusion
targets.note: The subcategory needs ContainsZero and IsClosedUnderBinaryProducts; the split and canonical structures are distinct data.

targets.target: Free abelian group on Shrink (Skeleton C) with class maps invariant under isomorphism, induction and lift principles stated over objects of C
targets.note: ObjectCode C is Shrink (Skeleton C); every K₀ of the roadmap is an instance of PresentedK0.

targets.target: Relations as generated subgroups, quotient universal property for isomorphism-invariant functions satisfying the relations, and extensionality on object classes
targets.note: FreeAbelianGroup (ObjectCode C) ⧸ closure of a set of relations.

targets.target: Choice independence: canonical isomorphisms between two skeleton/small-model presentations characterized by class maps, with naturality and cocycle laws
targets.note: `PresentedK0.mapEquiv` takes essentially small categories in independent smallness universes w, w' and any equivalence carrying the chosen relations both ways; with the identity equivalence it compares the presentations of one category in two universes, which is the only choice left because `ObjectCode C = Shrink.{w} (Skeleton C)` is determined by C and w. It is characterized on object classes (`mapEquiv_of`), with identity and cocycle laws (`mapEquiv_refl`, `mapEquiv_trans`), and split, exact and triangulated K₀ have the same `mapEquiv`. Missing: a named choice-independence comparison and its naturality with respect to `map`.

targets.target: Compatibility with product categories and finite biproducts; functors additive in each variable yield bilinear maps on K₀
targets.note: Biadditive invariants descend for exact K₀ (and the tensor product gives a ring structure on split K₀). Missing: K₀ of product categories and biadditive descent for split, triangulated or generic presented K₀.

targets.target: Split K₀: biproduct relations, induction, universal property, functoriality for additive functors, equivalence invariance, comparison with Mathlib group completion
targets.note: The comparison identifies Algebra.GrothendieckAddGroup of the isomorphism-class monoid with SplitK0 (needs a zero object).

targets.target: Exact K₀ for an exact structure: universal property for conflation-additive invariants, functoriality for conflation-exact functors, exact equivalences, canonical comparison from split K₀ with naturality
targets.note: Also fromSplit_surjective and map_comp_fromSplit.

targets.target: Abelian K₀ defined as exact K₀ of the canonical structure, with ShortExact lemmas, functoriality for exact functors and equivalence invariance
targets.note: Not a second presentation, as the layer requires.

targets.target: Triangulated K₀: triangle-additive universal property, maps from triangulated functors with naturality, equivalence invariance, split triangles, [0] = 0 and [X[n]] = (−1)^n[X]
targets.note: Also of_zero, of_biprod (split triangles) and fromSplit, for an essentially small pretriangulated category.

targets.target: Compatibility of triangulated K₀ with products
targets.note: No product-category statement for any K₀ in the Tau Ceti GrothendieckGroup directory.

targets.target: Bounded-complex comparisons: split K₀(A) ≅ triangulated K₀ of K^b(A); in abelian K₀ the class of a bounded complex is the alternating sum of homology classes; the bounded derived category comparison
targets.note: The Euler–Poincaré identity in abelian K₀ is present. Missing: the isomorphism with triangulated K₀ of the bounded homotopy category (Mathlib has no K^b) and the D^b comparison.

targets.target: Graded exact categories (shift autoequivalence {1}), graded conflation-exact functors and equivalences, graded split/exact/abelian/triangulated K₀ with the ℤ-action and shift-compatible universal property, and the forgetful map to ungraded K₀
targets.note: The forgetful map is ExactK0.map along the forgetful functor, shown shift-invariant; that it is not an isomorphism in general is recorded in prose, as the layer asks. SplitK0, AbelianK0 and TriangulatedK0 carry shiftZPow too.

targets.target: Finite P-resolutions as finite chains of conflations, with length, truncation, transport under isomorphism, zero padding, direct sums and the object property of admitting one
targets.note: Recursive presentation with ofIso, pad and admitsFiniteResolution_induction.

targets.target: Equivalence of the recursive, bounded exact augmented complex and object-property presentations, matched with Mathlib finite-resolution API
targets.note: A finite projective resolution in the abelian structure gives Mathlib projective dimension bounds; the complex presentation and its comparison with the recursive one are missing.

targets.target: Resolving subcategories: repleteness, zero and biproduct closure, extension closure, closure under kernels of admissible epimorphisms, finite P-resolutions of all objects, explicit induced exact structure
targets.note: No resolving-subcategory package (grep IsResolving, "resolving subcategor" finds only docstrings); extension closure and ambient kernel closure exist separately.

targets.target: Euler class of a finite resolution: independence of length, padding and choice, and additivity on conflations by the common-refinement argument for general resolving P
targets.note: Invariance under isomorphism, zero padding and direct sums holds for every extension-closed P containing zero and closed under binary biproducts (`eulerClassFullSubcategory_ofIso`, `_zeroPad`, `_pad`, `_biprod`). Independence of the choice of resolution and additivity on conflations are proved only for P consisting of E-projectives (Schanuel and horseshoe); the file docstring states that the general resolving case via the common-refinement argument is not carried out. The ambient-K₀ class is independent for trivial telescoping reasons.

targets.target: Resolution theorem: under resolving hypotheses the inclusion induces an isomorphism on exact K₀ with inverse the alternating resolution class, natural in compatible exact functors and invariant under equivalence
targets.note: Only P ≤ E.isProjective (closed under zero and biproducts, essentially small) is covered, with both inverse identities; naturality, equivalence invariance and the general resolving case are missing.

targets.target: Projective horseshoe lemma and Schanuel lemma in exact categories
targets.note: Mathlib has no horseshoe lemma.

targets.target: Comparison maps from a resolution to a fixed projective resolution, unique up to chain homotopy, under enough projectives
targets.note: Mathlib has comparison maps and homotopy uniqueness for projective resolutions in abelian categories; nothing for FiniteResolution in exact categories and no bridge between the two.

targets.target: Graded resolutions: graded finite P-resolutions, graded resolving subcategories, graded Euler class and resolution theorem, graded comparison and horseshoe, agreement with ungraded Euler classes at q = 1
targets.note: grep GradedResolution, "graded resolution", GradedFiniteResolution returns nothing.

targets.target: Linear graded projective resolutions over algebras generated in degrees 0 and 1: equivalence with diagonal Ext vanishing and with inverse graded Cartan/Poincaré series under q ↦ −q; linear resolutions are minimal
targets.note: grep IsKoszul, linearResolution, "diagonal Ext", PoincareSeries finds nothing relevant in either tree.

duplicates.note: K.3 proves the resolution theorem for a full exact resolving subcategory with its closure and finite-resolution hypotheses and constructs the degree-zero alternating-resolution inverse, which is the general resolving case of this layer.

targets.target: K₀(proj A) and G₀(mod A) through Layers 2–3, with Morita and algebra-equivalence invariance
targets.note: Both groups exist as exact K₀ for any ring (finitely generated projectives carry the split structure). No Morita or algebra-equivalence invariance of these groups is stated.

targets.target: Bases: indecomposable projective classes form a basis of K₀(proj A) and simple classes a basis of G₀(mod A)
targets.note: The simple basis exists for any Artinian ring and an exhaustive family of pairwise nonisomorphic simples; the projective basis is missing.

targets.target: The projective/simple multiplicity pairing ⟨[P_i],[M]⟩ = [M:S_i] and its perfectness in the indexed bases
targets.note: The multiplicity coordinate [M : S] on G₀ exists; the pairing with K₀(proj A) and its perfectness do not.

targets.target: dim_k Hom_A(P_i, M) = dim_k End_A(S_i) · [M : S_i], its diagonal specialization, and identification with raw Hom dimension under split hypotheses
targets.note: Proved for a projective cover P of a simple module S over any k-algebra, with P and M finite-dimensional over k (Webb 7.4.1); the diagonal and off-diagonal values need no finiteness, and the split form assumes End_A(S) one-dimensional (automatic over an algebraically closed field).

targets.target: The Cartan map c_A : K₀(proj A) → G₀(mod A) induced by the inclusion
targets.note: Defined for any ring R with finitely generated modules.

targets.target: Cartan matrix in the projective/simple bases with (i,j) entry [P_j : S_i], comparison with the quiver roadmap Cartan matrix and the transpose conventions
targets.note: CartanMap.lean states that nothing there computes a Cartan matrix; Jordan–Hölder multiplicities and path-algebra Hom dimensions exist.

targets.target: Under finite finitely generated projective resolutions (e.g. finite global dimension) c_A is an isomorphism with inverse the alternating resolution class
targets.note: The hypothesis is that every finitely generated module has a finite resolution by finitely generated projectives, for any ring. Mathlib has projective dimension of objects of an abelian category (`projectiveDimension`, `HasProjectiveDimensionLE`), but neither library defines global dimension or derives that hypothesis from a finite one.

targets.target: Graded Cartan map K₀^gr(proj A) → G₀^gr(mod A) over the shift action, graded Cartan matrix with entries ∑_d q^d [P_j : S_i{d}], recovery of the ungraded map at q = 1, relation to inverse graded Poincaré matrix

review.notes: Checked all 281 targets. Mechanically: all 43 batch layers are present with no extras; the 444 distinct citations (497 uses) resolve at their file and line in declarations.tsv, or in source for four priority-100/90 instances, with namespaces confirmed by a comment-stripping resolver; none is private or deprecated and no cited file contains sorry or an axiom. Every present and partial target was read at source with its variable lines and hypotheses, by me or by one of five search agents whose findings I re-verified at source before using them. Every absent target was searched again by concept in declarations.tsv and both trees; I re-ran the standard-name searches myself for residual finiteness of free groups, symplectic bases, Koszul complexes, unbounded K-injective replacements, presentable adjoint functor theorems, Sylow images under surjections, the p-adic logarithm and the splitting of ℤ_pˣ, the linear topology of ℤ_[p], and repleteness.
